description:
Events, dated performances, series, seasons and festival structure in the catalog service; tenant-aware entities.

**Conditions of Success:**
- Organizer can model a single show, a run, a series/season and a festival skeleton via API
- Publishing lifecycle (draft/published/archived) with domain events
- Every entity carries organizer/tenant id (ADR-002)

Lineage: docs/product/brief.md · docs/product/prd-v1.md (capability map).

**Amended (grilling):** per ADR-005, performances, festival days and park operating days are all dated slots in one model; the catalog's slot abstraction must be pressure-tested against re-entry, mid-day capacity changes and weather closures during planning.

comments.body: COS defined at epic level. Not yet decomposed — US-stories are created when the owner prioritizes this epic (Gate 1), per PRD 'Capability map'.
Backlog grilling 2026-07-12 (owner decisions): unified dated-slot admission model (ADR-005) governs this epic's core abstraction.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
Decomposed 2026-07-14 at Gate-1 prioritization (owner: head of M2). Scope confirmed with the owner: **catalog structure + generalize the dated-slot model** (re-entry / mid-day capacity / weather closures pressure-tested as slot attributes); full festival/park *verticals* stay in TKT-14/TKT-13/TKT-12.

Five children (PRD: docs/product/prd-v1.md `## TKT-2` section):
- **TKT-49 · US-007** — Archived lifecycle state + `performance.archived` domain event (prefactor; extends TKT-26 publish). No blockers.
- **TKT-50 · US-008 (SPIKE, risk:low)** — Pressure-test the ADR-005 slot model → ADR-005 amendment + the decided attribute set/state machine. No blockers; blocks TKT-51.
- **TKT-51 · US-009** — Generalize `performance` → typed slot (`performance|festival_day|operating_day` + attributes); M1 flow migrates unchanged. Blocked-by TKT-50, TKT-49.
- **TKT-52 · US-010** — Series (run) + season grouping; series-level publish/archive fan-out. Blocked-by TKT-49.
- **TKT-53 · US-011** — Festival skeleton over shared-capacity `festival_day` slots (TKT-14 consumes). Blocked-by TKT-51, TKT-52.

Dependency DAG (blocked-by): 51→{50,49}; 52→49; 53→{51,52}. Cycle check: acyclic (49,50 are roots; every path terminates). Context-mémo baked per child (ADR-005 verbatim as the load-bearing binding, + ADR-002/004/009/003 per story), captured 2026-07-14.

Recommended claim order once prioritized: **TKT-50 (spike, unblocks the schema) and TKT-49 (prefactor) first** — both P0/P1 with zero blockers and the most unblocking power — then TKT-51, TKT-52, and finally TKT-53.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### ✅ Implementation readiness — PASS
| Criterion | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Quality gates extracted | ✅ | make check + contract-drift + ADR-004 tier + browser-verify appended to every child |
| Each child a vertical slice, ~1 PR | ✅ | create-via-API → event → storefront read, demoable alone; TKT-51 keeps the M1 flow green as its load-bearing signal |
| Prefactoring split out first | ✅ | TKT-49 (archived lifecycle) is the prefactor US-009/US-010 build on; TKT-50 spike de-risks the schema before it hardens |
| Ordered by dependency, no forward dep | ✅ | DAG 51→{50,49}, 52→{49}, 53→{51,52}; cycle check passed (acyclic) |
| AC verifiable everywhere | ✅ | idempotency codes, 409 reasons, deterministic event ids, migrate-unchanged regression, browser-verified grouping — no "works correctly" |
| Children linked + edges + cycle check | ✅ | parent=TKT-2 on all five; blocked-by edges wired; acyclic |
| Context-mémo baked per child | ✅ | ADR-005 verbatim (load-bearing) + per-story ADR-002/004/009/003; capturedAt 2026-07-14 |
| No unvalidated assumption a child silently depends on | ⚠️ | The slot attribute set is *assumed* until TKT-50 lands — made explicit: TKT-51 is blocked-by the spike, so nothing hardens on an unproven shape |

**Concerns:** none blocking. Two eyes-open notes for the owner:
1. **TKT-53 (US-011) shared-festival-capacity is the riskiest slice** — the catalog/inventory boundary for shared capacity is decided by the TKT-50 spike and only *expressed* here; the actual claim mechanics are TKT-4/TKT-14. If the spike surfaces that shared capacity needs inventory-side design first, TKT-53 may need to wait on a TKT-4 slice rather than ship as pure catalog skeleton. Flagged in the deferred open-items list.
2. **TKT-52 (US-010) is the largest child** — series + season + grouped public reads + storefront + series-level publish fan-out. If Planning finds it exceeds ~400 lines, split season-level aggregation into a follow-up slice (series first, season second); both stay vertical.

**Verdict:** PASS — the decomposition is sized, dependency-ordered, acyclic, gated, and context-baked; the one real risk (the slot abstraction) is quarantined behind the TKT-50 spike by construction. Ready for the owner to prioritize (Gate 1). The board will hard-block dragging TKT-51/52/53 to Ready until their blockers are Done, so TKT-49 and TKT-50 are the only immediately claimable children.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
**Admin-UI boundary (owner decision 2026-07-14):** TKT-2 ships the catalog **API + storefront (buyer-facing) reads** only — no organizer/back-office authoring UI, matching the M1 precedent (TKT-26/US-002: "creation via API only"). The organizer-facing **catalog builder UI** (authoring events, series, seasons, festivals and the US-009 slot kinds) is owned by **TKT-22 — Back office & staff RBAC**, whose COS is "organizer builds a sellable event end-to-end in the UI without API calls." Rationale: build one coherent builder surface over a stable catalog API, behind the staff identity/RBAC that TKT-22 owns, rather than front-running RBAC with a throwaway admin screen here. Consequence: at PO Review, TKT-2 children are validated via API + storefront output, not a click-through admin flow. TKT-22 is therefore a downstream consumer of this epic's API — cross-referenced there.

<!-- sdlc:stage=done kind=metrics -->
### Closeout — TKT-2 (Catalog & event structure)

Closed on 2026-08-08 during board validation, which found every child Done while the epic itself
still sat in Backlog. Epics carry no stage durations of their own — the work is in the children.

**19 / 19 children Done:** TKT-49, 50, 51, 52, 53, 58, 59, 60, 61, 62, 63, 64, 65, 66, 68, 69, 70,
71, 94.

**learnings:**
- The epic-closing step has no owner in this pipeline. Four epics (TKT-1, 5, 6, 35) were closed as
  their children finished; this one was not, and nothing detected the difference for as long as it
  sat there. The board's rollup makes the condition visible but nothing acts on it.
- This epic produced the densest ADR cluster in the repo — ADR-017 through ADR-020 (event schema
  evolution, slot transition concurrency, read-path scoping, index build concurrency) all trace to
  children here, and all four are now cited as required reading in `AGENTS.md`. TKT-61 in particular
  shipped an ordering bug twice, past a mutation-checked suite and a full review pass, which is why
  ADR-017 §5b′ exists.

**retro:** an all-children-Done epic that is not itself Done is mechanically detectable from the
board data. Worth a check in the skill's validation step rather than waiting for a human to notice
— the same check would have caught TKT-4's missing parent links, which hid that epic's real state
in the opposite direction.
